newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 24.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Austrim group yesterday launched a A$58 million takeover bid for industrial services group Hawker Richardson. The move is seen as the latest in a confident A$300 million acquisition drive by the company over the past year which has seen five different textile and plant hire companies added to Austrim's holdings. Page 19.

The New South Wales Treasury Corporation (NSW TCorp) has begun a comprehensive review of its A$3.5 billion Hourglass fund, which over 80 NSW Government instrumentalities invest their surplus funds in. NSW TCorp has retained consulting firm InTech Asset Consulting to provide advice on restructuring the firm to improve its efficiency. Page 19.

Australian brewing giant Carlton & United Breweries and small Tasmanian brewer J. Boag & Son are locked in a legal dispute over the distribution of the Cascade beer brand in Tasmania. The State Supreme Court will resume the case this Friday to hear allegtions by J. Boag & Son that CUB is hindering it from marketing and distributing Cascade. Page 19.

The management of Government-owned contracting company Hunter Watertech has purchased the business from the New South Wales Government in a A$7 million buyout. Managing director Paul Chisholm said the operation has expanded beyond the capacities of the previous managing body, the Hunter Water Corporation, and that privatisation would allow for further growth. Page 23.

Perth-based gold miner Metex Ltd is set to float its Victorian gold exploration assets and create a new company called Vicgold NL, which will combine Metex's existing Victorian assets with exploration assets presently owned by unlisted company Greater Benigo Gold Mines Ltd. The move is designed to exploit interest aroused by recent geological data gathered by aeromagnetic surveys across the State which show promising mineral deposits. Page 22.

Western Australian junior gold miner Kilkenny Gold NL KYD.AX is hoping its A$23 million take-over bid for Kalmet Resources NL will expand its role in the State's gold industry. The move, announced yesterday, will combine Kalmet's 419,000-ounce Maud Creek gold poject in the Northern Territory with Kilkenny's many exploration projects. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Plastics and chemicals group ICI Australia has been laid open to a possible take-over by its parent shareholder Imperial Chemical Industries Plc's decision to offer a A$2.3 billion global offering of ICI Australia shares. ICI Plc group strategic planning manager Robert Milligan said yesterday there would be no restrictions placed on the amount of shares any individual or business could obtain in the offer. Page 21.

Telecommunications company Spectrum Network Systems is poised for its entry into the Australian market after the full deregulation of the sector on July 1. Spectrum is a fixed-line and mobile phone service provider and is anticipating troubles with industry giant Telstra as the latter attempts to continue its market dominance of telecommunications services. Page 21.
Conservationist John Wamsley is hoping to raise

approximately A$3 million for his Earth Sanctuaries group of wildlife refuges following the release of the firm's latest prospectus. Earth Sanctuaries is a public but unlisted company with 1500 shareholders and is now offering five million ordinary shares at A$1.50 each. Page 22.

Australian mining company Alcaston Mining NL has combined with Canada's Poplar Resources to advance its effort to gain diamond exploration rights in Sweden. Alcaston has been fighting legal battles in Sweden since 1994 in an attempt to establish its righs over diamond exploration projects in the country's north. Page 22.

Australian company Petroz NL announced yesterday it has found gas deposits in the Hingkip-1 well to the north of its Bayu-Undan gas condensate field in the Timor Sea. Petroz exploration manager Al Haydock said yesterday the find was higher in liquids tha any previously within Bayu-Undan. Page 23.

Hungry Jack's fast food chain owner Jack Cowin spoke out yesterday on the need for Australian business to explore energy efficiency technology. Hungry Jack's, along with fellow fast food outlets McDonald's and Domino's Pizza, have combined with the New Suth Wales Sustainable Energy Development Authority in a project which aims to generate a 20 per cent internal rate of return from investments in energy efficiency from a trial of 150 premises State-wide. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Reg Grundy's RG Capital is lobbying the Federal Government to make the proposed sixth free to air television channel a commercial network and has offered A$250 million for the operating licence. RG Capital's managing director Tim Hughes said yesterday that as the other television networks made over A$400 million annually he believed there was market room for another capital city TV network. Page 27

Today is the last chance for Westpac Banking Corp to agree to further concessions to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission in order to secure approval for its A$1.4 billion take-over bid for the Bank of Melbourne. The new concessions are expcted to concentrate on Wesptac's planned sell-off of approximately 80 branches to banking rivals like St George Bank and Suncorp-Metway Bank MWB.AX. Page 29.

The Federal Government's plans to sell the AIDC investment bank by the end of the financial year have been postponed with the Government delaying the announcement of the successful bidder until late next month. In preparation for privatisation the AIDC board has been revamped with professional director Malcolm Irving being appointed chairman, and two new directors, Jim Wright from the Department of Industry, Science and Tourism and independent businessman Tony Sherlock, being instated. Page 29.

The Australian Federal Treasury is drawing up a new set of rules to police capitalisation of Australian businesses by foreign companies. Duncan Baxter, an international tax partner with Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu, says the new rules will reduce the extent to which a foreign parent company can capitalise an Australian subsidiary with debt rather than equity. Page 31.

Funds under management by Tyndall Australia have increased by A$200 million in the first five and a half calendar months of 1997, already equalling the whole of funds growth for 1996. Consulting company InTech's recent survey of fund managers active in the Australian sharemarket reveals Tyndall to have been a stellar performer over the last five years. Page 32.

The latest Business Stress Index for the March quarter, released yesterday, revealed that continued poor retail trading has resulted in a trebling in the number of forced sales of retail and wholesale traders. Accounting firm Ernst & Young found that half of these sales occurred in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory. Page 27.
THE AGE

Unless the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission improves its accountability to the public and the transparency of its investigations it risks being subjected to a parliamentary inquiry. This warning was delivered following a parliamentary reviewof the ACCC's 1995-96 annual report. Page B1.

The National Australia Bank is the first big Australian bank to introduce touch-screen terminals, which use multi-media technology and video conferencing to market the bank's financial services products. Page B3.

Australis Media shares rose by 8 per cent after media giants Foxtel and PBL agreed to equalise their local pay TV interests. Meanwhile, Australis director Nick Falloon, who is also the finance director at Nine Network, has resigned from the board due to potential conflict of interests. Page B3.

Shares in PBR Automotive (Malaysia) have been bought out by parent company Pacific BBA for an undisclosed sum and will be held until a new joint-venture partner is found. Pacific BBA has two years to find a new partner as Malaysia's investment rules requiRe foreign companies to anchor their investments with local joint-venture partners. Page B3.

The accounting and legal professions are lobbying Opposition and independent senators to reject a Government bill which seeks to plug a loophole in the tax laws that benefited alcoholic mixers such as Carlton & United's Subzero Alcoholic Soda. Page B3.

The Arthur Yates group is planning to cut staff numbers by 12 per cent due to diffcult trading conditions in the garden-supplies market and tough pricing competition. Yates also intends to sell three properties worth about $3 million as part of the reorgaisation effort. Page B2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
